message.content:
In Blackjack, the Ace is the most flexible card in the deck because it can be counted as either **1** or **11**, depending on which value gives your hand the best chance of winning without going over 21.

### How it works

| Situation | Value used |
|-----------|------------|
| You’re dealt an Ace alone | 11 (unless you already have a hard 10 or higher) |
| You have an Ace plus other cards | 11 if the total ≤ 21; otherwise 1 |
| Two Aces together | 12 (one counts as 11, the other as 1) |
| Three Aces | 13 (two count as 1, one as 11) |
| Four Aces | 14 (all count as 1) |

The dealer will automatically adjust the Ace’s value to avoid busting. If you have a “soft” hand (an Ace counted as 11), you can still hit safely because the Ace will switch to 1 if needed.

### Splitting Aces

* You may split a pair of Aces into two separate hands.
* After splitting, each new hand receives only **one additional card** (no further hits allowed on those split Aces in many casinos).

### Summary

* **Primary role:** Ace can be 1 or 11, whichever keeps the hand from busting.
* **Special rules:** Splitting Aces is allowed but limited to one extra card per split hand.

That’s the core rule for Aces in Blackjack!
